title: Unify benchmark scaffold, upgrade core dependencies, and harden regression signals
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket consolidates multiple ad-hoc benchmarking scaffolds into a single maintainable harness, updates pinned dependency versions that block async and multi-GPU runners, and improves regression signal quality so perf regressions are caught earlier with less noise.
background: Over the past 24 months we have accumulated several benchmarking entry points: an older pytest-based smoke runner, a Go-based long-run harness, and the eval CI scripts used by research. Each has slightly different scenario schema and metrics plumbing. Several key dependencies (grpcio, aiohttp, numpy, and our internal loadgen library) are pinned to older versions that prevent moving to the new async batchers and KV-cache optimizations. This causes duplicated maintenance effort and flaky alerts during release validation.
goals: Replace 3 legacy entry points with one unified benchmark scaffold that supports sync and async runners
Upgrade grpcio, aiohttp, numpy, and internal-loadgen to latest compatible versions and validate on CI
Standardize scenario manifest schema and implement a migration tool for existing scenarios
Reduce false positives in perf-regression alerts by improving baseline selection and smoothing logic
Add a lightweight canary smoke job that runs on every staging deploy to catch obvious regressions quickly
non_goals: Full rewrite of existing load generators — we will adapterize legacy runners instead
Implementing new ML model evaluation metrics (outside scope of harness infra)
Large-scale optimization of individual kernels — focus is harness stability and observability
success_metrics: Single canonical benchmark CLI + runner used by CI and dev teams within 6 weeks
Dependency upgrades merged and deployed without CI flakiness within 2 sprints
Perf-regression alert noise reduced by >=60% (measured over 30-day window)
Canary smoke job reduces mean time to detect major regressions from deployment from hours to <30m
risks: Upgrading grpcio/aiohttp could expose subtle incompatibilities in internal RPC middleware
Consolidation may temporarily break existing dashboards if metric names change
Adapters for legacy runners could miss edge-case scenario semantics leading to drift in historical baselines
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Audit existing entry points and produce a compatibility matrix (1 week)
Phase 2: Design canonical scenario manifest and migration tool; get design review (1 week)
Phase 3: Implement unified CLI + pluggable runner interface; adapterize pytest & Go harnesses (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Upgrade dependencies in a separated branch, run expanded CI across staging hardware, fix regressions (2 weeks)
Phase 5: Integrate canary smoke job into staging and add smoothing/aggregation improvements to regression detector (1 week)
Phase 6: Documentation, runbook, and handover to SRE and QE; deprecate legacy entry points (1 week)
milestones: M4: Dependencies upgraded in staging and smoke pass green - 2025-03-19
M5: Canary smoke job live and alerting tuned - 2025-03-22
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for manifest parser and adapter layer
Integration tests that run canonical scenarios end-to-end on a small GPU pool
Backfill historical runs against migrated manifests to validate baseline parity
Run dependency-upgrade matrix across Ubuntu18/20 images and on-host CUDA variants used by Dedicated
Observability checks: ensure token-level latency histograms and per-route cost signals are intact
docs_and_handovers: Runbook: how to add a new scenario and how to interpret regression alerts
Demo session scheduled for Platform and QE teams after M4
Deprecation notices and links to adapter usage examples for legacy scripts
